description:
Port the Distributor from feature/q67-phase-a onto the current architecture, ADAPTED to keyspace-mutation publication. The branch (former PR #97) is the audited reference implementation and is deleted once this lands. Source studies (2026-08-21): FDB DD ownership model (MoveKeys lock, dual-index write protocol, recovery non-interaction) and the phase-a inventory (what ports / must-not-port / valid test specs) — both summarized in this ticket's design basis below.

SETTLED COURSE (with the user, 2026-08-21):
(A) LIFETIME: director-recruited per epoch initially (phase-a supervision ports near-verbatim: recruit-if-absent, halt registration losers, :normal DOWN = ceded); the LOCK, not the supervisor, is the write authority, so graduating to cross-epoch later is non-breaking.
(B) RECOVERY becomes read-and-heal with a tag-0 carve-out: persistence stops blanket clear+rewrite; shard_keys seeds only-when-absent (boundaries never change without splits); materializers seeds-when-absent + writes exactly what recovery changed; tag 0 stays recovery's job (stall-only-for-tag-0); data-tag gaps become the distributor's to heal (bootstrap keeps creating data-tag workers until phase 4, then leaves gaps ABSENT for placeholder coverage).
(C) PLACEHOLDER ADDRESSING: the placeholder IS a materializer ref — the distributor writes materializers/<tag> = {placeholder_worker_id, distributor_node}; the placeholder speaks the materializer read API; nothing changes at proxy or client; coverage gaps are visible in the keyspace. (The phase-a pid-in-TSL-slot mechanism must not port.)
(D) CURRENT-SCALE SCOPE: failure monitoring + per-tag coverage check + ONE mutating op (heal under check_lock). Premature until moves/replicas: serverKeys dual index, teams, relocation queue, throttles, shard metrics.
(E) IN-BAND RETIREMENT: healing introduces mid-epoch removals, un-deferring the q67.38 obligation — the proxy's apply-then-route dual-routes the membership change to the victim's own shard stream (FDB privatization) so a displaced-but-alive worker self-retires; built only after heal exists. The q67.44 client-cache overlap obligation does NOT activate here (heals change refs, not boundaries; waits for splits).

FENCING (the load-bearing mechanism): port of FDB's MoveKeys lock — distributor_lock/{owner,write} system keys; take-then-snapshot on start; read-check-write inside every mutating transaction (every write proves in its own serializable commit that no newer owner appeared); 5s read-only poll-to-die. Commit abort replaces the phase-a delta-rejection as both the supersession signal and the orphan-cleanup trigger.

PHASES (child tickets, dependency-wired): q67.21.1 lock — q67.21.2 recovery reads-and-heals — q67.21.3 singleton + placeholder-as-ref — q67.21.4 recruit/heal transactions under lock — q67.21.5 idle spin-down + re-adoption residue — q67.21.6 in-band retirement. Splits/moves are a future arc (start/finish dual-write with in-flight dest marker; new-distributor rule: re-enqueue anything with a dest).

MUST-NOT-PORT from phase-a (exhaustive, from the inventory): Director.apply_tsl_delta and all call sites; placeholder-pid-into-TSL-slot anywhere; TSL snapshots as distributor inputs; Recruitment.shard_tsl/filter_logs_for_shard (unlock takes typed pull_sources now); the distributor monitor map as coverage source-of-truth (the committed materializers/ family is authoritative). PORTS IN SPIRIT: demand channel with per-tag dedupe, bounded parking (min(client timeout, hold_ms), shed :unavailable), recruitment pipeline (Foreman seams, lock at epoch, unlock at worker-reported durable version), director re-recruitment semantics, idle spin-down, re-adoption RESIDUE only (the durable materializers/ family already feeds bootstrap re-adoption; porting it whole would double-adopt). The phase-a placeholder/recruitment/healing/spindown/readoption test files remain the behavior spec, re-targeted from TSL-delta observations to committed-mutation observations and rebuilt on by-key proxy resolution.

Blocked by bedrock-q67.20 (landed on the integration branch). Unblocks bedrock-q67.9's exit criterion.

comments.text: Audit 2026-08-20 (post trim campaign, stacks #161/#166 collapsed into feature/q67-phase-b-prereqs @ 3862a5b2): three references in this ticket are now stale. (1) 'family + encoding already exist' - no longer true: q67.31 deleted the MaterializerList codec and every unread system-key family under the 'a key without a reader is inventory, not communication' rule. materializer_keys/ returns WITH this ticket, writer and reader landing together, shaped by what the reader needs. (2) 'resolver->window->CommitProxy.Metadata pipeline' - CommitProxy.Metadata was deleted (q67.30); the pipeline's consumer is RoutingData (immutable gb_trees), applied under the serialized apply-then-route gate (q67.24). Window application is now the exact per-proxy relay (q67.33), fail-fast, converged-verdict (q67.22) - stronger than what this ticket assumed. (3) 'whichever read path q67.9 picks' - settled on q67.9 2026-08-20: FDB serves GetKeyServerLocations from proxies out of keyInfo; Bedrock's analogue is the proxy's RoutingData snapshot. This ticket lands the writer + healing loop against that. The PersistencePhase ownership question stands and should be answered by the q67.23 decision (seeded recover_from).

Deferred obligation from the 2026-08-20 side-channel campaign design: when the Distributor introduces mid-epoch materializer removal, retirement delivery goes IN-BAND, FDB-style - the proxy's apply-then-route step dual-routes a membership clear (materializers/<tag>) to the victim's own shard tag so the worker observes its own key cleared in the stream it already follows and self-retires (ApplyMetadataMutation.cpp privatization -> storageserver applyPrivateData worker_removed). Until then, retirement is recovery-boundary-only via foreman rejoin validation (course B). Do not build the private-mutation path before removals exist.

Obligation from the PR #182 audit (2026-08-20): the client-side LayoutIndex partial cache assumes shard-range disjointness, which holds today because recovery's per-epoch rewrite is the only boundary writer and invalidation is coarse. When the Distributor introduces mid-epoch boundary mutations, superseded ranges can coexist with their replacements in a live index with no invalidation trigger — the insert must become overlap-aware (or eviction per-range) BEFORE mid-epoch splits/moves land. Flagged in the LayoutIndex moduledoc.

SETTLED with the user 2026-08-21 (supersedes open questions in earlier comments; based on the FDB DD source study + phase-a reference inventory, both 2026-08-21): (A) Distributor is director-recruited PER EPOCH initially (phase-a supervision ports near-verbatim: recruit-if-absent, halt losers, :normal DOWN = ceded); the LOCK, not the supervisor, is the write authority, so graduating to cross-epoch later is non-breaking. (B) Recovery becomes read-and-heal with a tag-0 carve-out: persistence stops blanket clear+rewrite; shard_keys seeds only-when-absent (first boot); materializers seeds-when-absent + writes exactly what recovery changed; tag 0 stays recovery's job (stall-only-for-tag-0), data-tag gaps become the distributor's to heal (bootstrap keeps creating data-tag workers until phase 4, then leaves gaps ABSENT for placeholder coverage). (C) Placeholder addressing = OPTION 2: the placeholder IS a materializer ref - distributor writes materializers/<tag> = {placeholder_worker_id, distributor_node}; the placeholder speaks the materializer read API; nothing changes at proxy or client; coverage gaps are visible in the keyspace. (D) Current-scale distributor = failure monitoring + per-tag coverage check + ONE mutating op (heal under check_lock); NO serverKeys dual index, teams, relocation queue, throttles, shard metrics - all premature until moves/replicas. (E) Healing un-defers in-band retirement (first mid-epoch removal): privatized membership change dual-routed to the victim's own shard stream, phase 6. q67.44 overlap obligation does NOT activate (heals change refs, not boundaries; waits for splits). Ownership fencing = MoveKeys lock port: distributor_lock/{owner,write}, take-then-snapshot, read-check-write in every mutating transaction, 5s read-only poll-to-die.
